whyForBowfishing: Bowfishing is done at night with lights, and the darker the water the better the light cuts through it and the more the fish stand out. A bright moon washes that out; thick cloud cancels the moon, except near cities, where cloud reflects the city's glow back down. The score asks: does every lake get a darkness call for tonight that counts the cloud, and has a simple light reading shown the darkness classes come out in the right order?
measurement: Domain capability score (Cortex scoring.md SC-02, SC-03): how far Sector can trust the Moon and Night Light Brain's published on-water darkness class for tonight. Not operational health, not production readiness, not comparable with any other Brain's score.
question: Per lake, for tonight, does the Moon Brain publish a darkness call that counts the cloud (not only the clear-sky moon), for every lake it computes, and has a simple light reading shown the darkness classes come out in the right order (gap MOON-VAL-001)?
unknownPolicy: Unknown counts against the Brain everywhere (owner rule 2026-11-23: nothing should show unknown). A lake, tile or field that is unknown, unavailable, blocked or abstained earns 0 and stays in every denominator. Unknown is never rewarded or excluded to make a share look better. Every per-lake share therefore divides by ONE fixed denominator, all the lakes the Brain is meant to cover; a lake with no state (blocked, never computed, errored) is in it and earns 0. A Brain-level fact that is not published scores 0 and lowers completeness: both count as 0, never as excluded. Filling an unknown with an estimate is worse still: it is an invented value, which the validation checks fail, so the only way to remove an unknown is real data. For Moon, a night judged on the moon alone (basis MOON_ONLY: cloud unknown) is an unknown and counts against.
scope: Every per-lake share divides by the whole directory (/brains/moon.directoryLakeCount); a lake with no night state this run (errored, or not in the run) earns 0. Polar-day lakes (basis NO_NIGHT) have no night to judge and leave only the cloud share. Validation fleet-wide.
dimensionClasses: Cortex scoring.md SC-09: CAP, COV, PRED, VAL, ENG, VOL. This draft has no ENG or VOL dimension.
unscoredWhen: The registry /brains/moon is absent (the Brain has never published). The scorer then writes NO score block: UNSCORED, never 0. Registry presence, not lastSuccessfulRun, decides this: Moon writes lastSuccessfulRun null whenever any lake errors in a run (moon_brain/publish.py), so keying on it would make the score appear and disappear. A run with errors is scored and shows up in currentNight and the health gate. Today this holds (PARKED, no executor, run.py --write refuses without an APPROVED release and MOON_WRITE_APPROVED=1).

dimensions.label: Darkness class validated against measured on-water light (MOON-VAL-001)
dimensions.note: The sun, twilight and moon events are deterministic astronomy, already cross-checked against USNO in tests (moon-night-light-v1.json usnoCrossCheck). That cross-check is not published as a measurement, so it earns nothing here. The one judgement the Brain makes is the darkness class, so validation carries the largest weight.
dimensions.why: One simple light reading per night shows whether the darkness class matches how dark the water really is.

dimensions.label: Darkness class includes cloud cover
dimensions.note: MOON_ONLY (cloud unknown) and a lake with no basis at all (errored or not computed) earn nothing and stay in the denominator; only NO_NIGHT lakes (polar day) are left out, because there is no night to judge. Credit needs the Weather Brain live (MOON-INP-001) and Moon run after each evening Weather run (plan section 7.1). The fixed city-glow allowance is the Engine's; a per-lake skyglow input (MOON-INP-002) is not scored until it is published.
dimensions.why: Cloud cancels the moon except near cities, so a darkness call without cloud can call an overcast night bright.

dimensions.label: Lakes computed for tonight without error
dimensions.fact: sum of /brains/moon.breakdowns.basis (lakes with a night state this run) / /brains/moon.directoryLakeCount
dimensions.note: Counts lakes that got a darkness call this run over the whole directory, so an errored lake and a lake left out of the run both count against. Replaces a coverage dimension: Moon's supportedLakeCount is every lake in the run, errored ones included, so it measures nothing.
dimensions.why: A lake that could not be computed tonight has no darkness call; it counts against.

validationStatusMeaning.source: brains/moon/research/GAPS.json MOON-VAL-001 (stop condition: a preregistered comparison against an independent illuminance dataset, public sky-quality or lux records near fleet lakes, is scored). Unlike Weather and Generation, the Moon plan has NO pre-registered validation thresholds yet (MOON_BRAIN_PLAN.md section 7 item 3).
validationStatusMeaning.preRegistrationRequired: VALIDATED and PARTIAL both require the check (site, nights, reading method, pass rule) to be written down and committed BEFORE any reading is looked at. This rubric does not decide it.
validationStatusMeaning.statedProxy: Keep it practical. The truth is a simple light reading on real nights: a sky-quality meter or a phone light-meter app pointed straight up, at one fleet lake (a bowfisher's own readings are welcome) or a public sky-quality station near one. No multi-site statistical campaign is needed.
validationStatusMeaning.proposedCheck: PROPOSAL, for Michael to accept, change or reject, and to write down before any reading is taken: about 12 nights at one site, covering dark and bright moon and clear and cloudy skies. PASS if the average reading gets brighter with each class step (DARK, MOSTLY_DARK, SOME_MOONLIGHT, BRIGHT_MOON) and cloudy bright-moon nights read darker than clear bright-moon nights.
validationStatusMeaning.newInThisDraft: Everything in this block beyond the gap's stop condition is new: the practical proxy, the proposed check and the PARTIAL tier. All need the owner's approval, and the check is written down before any reading.
validationStatusMeaning.VALIDATED: The written-down check PASSES on both parts (class order and cloud cancelling the moon).
validationStatusMeaning.PARTIAL: The class-order part PASSES and the cloudy-night part is NOT YET SCORED (not enough cloudy nights yet); nothing FAILED.
validationStatusMeaning.NOT_VALIDATED: Anything else: no pre-registration, ANY criterion FAILED, or an insufficient sample. A FAIL produces a DARKNESS_RULE_V2 proposal with its own pre-registration; V1 results are kept and never credited.
validationStatusMeaning.whoSetsIt: The Moon Brain's validation record (a reviewed change that writes /validation/moon), never the scorer.
